subject.title: Unhandled Playwright assertion error in CRSession._onMessage crashes Gateway

question: Should this be fixed as a narrow browser-owned Playwright CDP assertion recovery path, or should maintainers require browser/CDP isolation in a child process or node host before closing this issue?
rationale: The source supports the crash class, but choosing between targeted in-process suppression and a broader crash-isolation boundary affects Gateway fatal-error policy, browser ownership, and session recovery behavior.

options.title: Narrow Browser Recovery First
options.body: Treat only proven Playwright CDP assertion leaks as recoverable browser-plugin failures, keep unknown unhandled rejections fatal, and require live CDP proof plus focused tests.

options.title: Require Process Isolation
options.body: Keep this issue open as an architecture task until browser/CDP operations run outside the main Gateway process and can reconnect without killing unrelated sessions.

options.title: Defer Pending Live Repro
options.body: Ask for a fresh current-main CRSession repro before choosing the permanent recovery boundary.

recommendation.title: Narrow Browser Recovery First
recommendation.body: Treat only proven Playwright CDP assertion leaks as recoverable browser-plugin failures, keep unknown unhandled rejections fatal, and require live CDP proof plus focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Gateway/browser fatal-error and Playwright dependency surfaces are most strongly connected to steipete in the available history.
